meta.title: Who really said "Invert, always invert"? | Quotle.info
meta.description: Munger repeated this maxim while crediting Jacobi. A contemporaneous Jacobi source has not been established.
meta.ogDescription: Munger repeated this maxim while crediting Jacobi. A contemporaneous Jacobi source has not been established.

answer.label: Credited by Munger to Jacobi
answer.sourceLine: In the 1996 talk Practical Thought About Practical Thought, Munger expressly attributes this maxim to Carl Jacobi. The reproduced talk confirms Munger’s use, but does not identify a contemporary Jacobi publication; Jacobi’s original wording and translation remain unverified.

author.name: Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi
author.heading: About Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi
author.bio: Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi was a German mathematician whose work ranged across analysis and algebra. Charlie Munger invoked him as a model of reversing a difficult problem to find a solution. The checked Munger text establishes that attribution without identifying a contemporary Jacobi source for the English maxim.

context.heading: The setting behind the words
lead: Munger uses inversion as one of five methods for solving difficult practical problems. His 1996 example explicitly sends readers back to the mathematician Jacobi, rather than presenting the maxim as his own coinage. The document establishes that chain of credit, but not a nineteenth-century German original. Munger talk reproduction ↗
